releaseName: Windows IaaS VMAgent 2.7.41491.1225 AMD64&ARM64 [Cancelled At Stage 9]
summary: Dry-run analysis of VMAgent 2.7.41491.1225 (baseline 2.7.41491.1216). This release exposes no downloadable .zip package assets on GitHub, so binary-level evidence (Authenticode signatures, PE/.NET target framework, OS-compatibility imports, embedded rustc versions) could not be collected; the assessment is therefore based on the published change list only. The change list is a routine feature/telemetry/build-infra update with no indication of a signing-certificate change, a move away from .NET Framework 4.0, or an OS-matrix change. It does touch Rust code paths (catalog-file install/uninstall), so the Rust compiler / OS supportability check must be re-run against the shipped Rust binaries once package assets are available. Overall risk is Low with several items pending binary verification.

findings.rationale: The change list includes PR 14499782 'Rust install and uninstall methods for catalog file feature' and PR 14786098 'catalog support', indicating the shipped Rust components changed in this release relative to 2.7.41491.1216.
findings.recommendation: Once the signed package is attached to the release, recover the embedded rustc version for each Rust binary and confirm it is < 1.78 so the Windows Server 2008 SP2 / Windows 7 SP2 baseline is preserved.

findings.finding: rustc version could not be recovered (no package assets)
findings.rationale: The release carries no downloadable .zip assets, so no Rust binary was available to fingerprint for its embedded rustc version. The rustc >= 1.78 -> Windows 10 / Server 2016 supportability rule could not be evaluated against actual binaries in this dry run.
findings.recommendation: Attach the signed release package and re-run the analysis to confirm the Rust binaries were built with rustc < 1.78 (or accept the raised baseline if >= 1.78).

findings.finding: Authenticode signatures could not be verified (no package assets)
findings.rationale: With no .dll/.exe/.sys binaries available to download, Get-AuthenticodeSignature could not be run, so signer subject/issuer/thumbprint/serial and any certificate drift vs. the baseline could not be checked.
findings.recommendation: Verify every shipped binary is validly Microsoft-signed and that the signing certificate (thumbprint / issuer / serial / algorithm / timestamp authority) is unchanged vs. 2.7.41491.1216 once assets are present.

findings.finding: Target framework could not be verified (no package assets)
findings.rationale: No managed assemblies were available to read the TargetFrameworkAttribute / PE metadata, so drift away from .NET Framework 4.0 could not be confirmed or ruled out. Nothing in the change list indicates a target-framework change.
findings.recommendation: Confirm all managed assemblies still target .NET Framework 4.0 when package assets are available.

findings.rationale: The change list records VMAgent-Shared 3.0.03312.64 -> 3.0.3355.67 and HostGAP-SDK 1.0.8.181 -> 1.0.8.184 (ProxyAgent-Shared unchanged). These are routine dependency bumps described as perf/telemetry optimizations and build-image upgrades.
findings.recommendation: Diff the shared-component binaries (size / version / hash) against the baseline once package assets are available.

findings.finding: Build image moved from 2019 to 2022 (build-time only)
findings.rationale: PR 15539952 'change build image from 2019 to 2022' and PR 15615349 'upgrade to 2022 image' change the build toolchain, not the runtime OS matrix. A newer toolchain can theoretically pull in newer imported APIs, but no runtime OS-matrix change is stated in the change list.
findings.recommendation: When binaries are available, inspect imported DLLs/APIs to ensure no symbols were introduced that are absent on Windows Server 2008 SP2 / Windows 7 SP2.

findings.finding: Feature/telemetry/validation changes with no compatibility signal
findings.rationale: The bulk of the change list is guest-agent pre-validation, signature-validation telemetry, static-check logic, goal-state performance improvements, binskim fixes and pipeline changes. None of these indicate a certificate change, a .NET target change, or an OS-matrix change.
findings.recommendation: No action beyond the standard binary verification once assets are attached.
